item.title: Perfect proof of "not all SCPs have to be grimdark"
item.content:encoded: Thank $DEITY for a break from killer side effects, world-ending threats, and monthly D-class terminations! Even the Foundation deserves to find an anomaly that's good clean fun (but not -J material) sometimes; the experiment logs were outstandingly well done, especially the "balanced budget" and "better key to happiness" wishes. Upvoted, wish I could legally upvote this skip more…

Upvoted, but there's one grammar thing:

Result: An used copy of Kerplunk

Since 'used' has a 'you' sound, it should be "a used copy'; if it was 'unused', which has an 'uh' sound, it would be 'An'. English is a dumb language.

item.content:encoded: I thought this was an excellent take on a wish-granting genie. This especially shines during the interview log, which was thoroughly enjoyable to read. Well done, +1.

Enjoyed this during crit, and still enjoy it now! It's a clever twist on your genie trope, well executed. I also feel there's additional stories to be told relating to the "Multiversal Interactions and Stability Administration"…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: One thing that really stood out to me is how the genie executes the "twist" on all of the wishes. In many other stories and works of fiction, the genie seems to be maliciously interpreting the wish as something extremely detrimental and/or fatal. The genie in the scip, on the other hand, just seems to make something disappointing, or not what the person expected. This almost bored seeming interpretation of the wish really sells the whole "interdimensional employee just doing his job". +1 Excellent execution

item.title: +1 wholeheartedly
item.content:encoded: The idea of a genie disrupted by red tape stopping them from correctly granting wishes is way too perfect. +1
